elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages ... for any delay in providing a dependency."
"shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages or penalties"

elements.element: Removal of the USD 25,000 per day liquidated sum
elements.evidence: operation replaces "USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages" with the negative operator

elements.element: Early-termination fee expressly capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: redline contains no early-termination fee or cap; clause reads "shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages or penalties"

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: no liquidated amount is preserved or designated as sole; "any liquidated damages or penalties" merely negated

reasons: The redline flips the operative obligation so no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer for dependency delay, satisfying both atomic elements of the preferred position at the locked target level.

Change is confined to the single sentence: the operator was negated and the USD 25,000 per-day figure removed; adding "or penalties" is necessary to cover the second preferred element and is not surplus.
No unrelated term, defined term, or surrounding mechanic is disturbed; the dependency-delay subject matter is retained so no dangling reference arises.
Fallback is not satisfied (no early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees), but that is irrelevant since the preferred level is fully met and the levels are separate bargains.
